text:
Carolina scored three times in a seven-minute stretch of the second period, and the scoreboard barely captured how lopsided the game had been. The Hurricanes carried the better chances from the opening faceoff, finishing with 3.23 expected goals to Philadelphia's 1.57 and outattempting the Flyers 59 to 41. Run the game's shots through a thousand simulated replays and Carolina wins 79 percent of them, so a 4-1 result was fair, if anything slightly kind to the home side.

The turn came at 10:16 of the second, when Andrei Svechnikov snapped one past Joseph Woll off a Sean Walker feed. Shayne Gostisbehere made it 2-0 at 13:45, and Christian Dvorak briefly gave Philadelphia life with a tip-in at 15:26. Carolina answered 88 seconds later. Sebastian Aho, set up by William Carrier and Svechnikov, restored the two-goal margin at 16:54, and the Flyers never got closer. Mark Jankowski added a snap shot at 15:09 of the third, the highest-quality chance of the five goals at 22 percent.

Neither team scored on the power play (Carolina went 0 for 4, Philadelphia 0 for 3), so even strength settled it, and Carolina owned that too at 2.86 expected goals against 1.40. Woll allowed four on roughly 3.2 expected, a modest shortfall, while Pyotr Kochetkov stopped 18 of 19 and slightly outperformed the shots he faced. Philadelphia hit more (20 to 13) and blocked twice as many shots (14 to 7), but all that effort mostly measured how often they were chasing.
